item.meaning: A scenario in barter where two traders each possess the exact item the other desires, enabling direct trade.
The function of money that allows it to serve as an accepted benchmark for settling future debts.

item.definition: An economic system of direct exchange of goods or services for other goods or services without using money.

item.description: Money serves four core economic roles: Medium of Exchange, Unit of Account, Store of Value, and Standard of Deferred Payment.

item.fact: The Junbeel Mela in Morigaon, Assam is an annual 3-day fair where hill tribes and plain farmers still practice traditional barter trade.

item.role_function: India's central banking authority holding legal sole right to mint, issue, and regulate currency notes.

stages: Barter System: Direct swap of goods (flawed by double coincidence of wants)
Commodity Money: Use of shells, salt, cattle, and grain as local value tools
Metallic Coinage: Stamped punch-marked silver/copper and gold coins
Paper Currency: Government/Central Bank backed paper bank notes
Digital Money: Electronic transfers, credit cards, UPI, and QR code payments

item.cause: Inherent limitations of barter (lack of double coincidence of wants and indivisibility)
item.effect: Drove human societies to invent commodity currency, metallic coins, paper money, and digital payment systems.

item.significance: The fundamental hurdle of barter requiring mutual matching of desires, solved by the invention of money.
